Name: Octave Mandolin
Description: Larger ancestor of the mandolin. Tuned an octave lower than the mandolin.

Name: Mandocello
Description: Larger ancestor of the mandolin. Tuned an octave lower than the standard mandola.

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer
Description: Also known as the Appalachian dulcimer, among other names. A fretted string instrument of the zither family. (Staff notation).

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer (tablature)
Description: Also known as the Appalachian dulcimer, among other names. A fretted string instrument of the zither family. (Tablature).

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer - Baritone
Description: Larger version of the mountain or Appalachian dulcimer. (Staff notation).

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer - Baritone (tablature)
Description: Larger version of the mountain or Appalachian dulcimer. (Tablature).

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer - Bass
Description: Very large mountain or Appalachian dulcimer, an octave lower than the regular dulcimer. (Staff notation).

Name: Mtn. Dulcimer - Bass (tablature)
Description: Very large mountain or Appalachian dulcimer, an octave lower than the regular dulcimer. (Tablature).

Name: Piccolo Balalaika
Description: Piccolo balalaika, tuned a fifth above the prima.
Prima balalaika. The most common balalaika.

Name: Prima Balalaika
Description: Prima balalaika. The most common balalaika.

Name: Secunda Balalaika
Description: Secunda balalaika, tuned a fifth below the prima.

Name: Alto Balalaika
Description: Alto balalaika, tuned an octave below the prima.

Name: Bass Balalaika
Description: Bass balalaika, tuned an octave below the alto.

Name: Contrabass Balalaika
Description: Contrabass balalaika, tuned an octave below the bass.

Name: Oud
Description: Short-neck lute-type fretless stringed instrument, common in the Middle East and North Africa.

Name: Shamisen
Description: Traditional Japanese three-stringed instrument played with a plectrum.

Name: Sitar
Description: Plucked string instrument used in Indian classical music.

Name: Prim
Description: The smallest tamburica, mostly used as a lead instrument.

Name: Brač
Description: A larger tamburica than the prim, played in a similar way.

Name: Bugarija
Description: A tamburica mostly used as a harmony/rhythm instrument.

Name: Berda
Description: The largest tamburica, used for playing bass lines.

Name: Čelo
Description: A tamburica similar in size to the bugarija, usually given counterpoint lines.

Name: Bandurria
Description: Spanish folk instrument similar to the mandolin. (Staff notation).

Name: Bandurria (tablature)
Description: Spanish folk instrument similar to the mandolin. (Tablature).

Name: Laúd
Description: Spanish lute similar to the bandurria. (Staff notation).

Name: Laúd (tablature)
Description: Spanish lute similar to the bandurria. (Tablature).

Name: Strings
Description: String section notated on a grand staff.

Name: Pardessus de viole
Description: Highest-pitched member of the viol family.

Name: Baryton
Description: Similar to the viol, but with an extra set of plucked strings.

Name: Violone
Description: Large viol with the lowest string tuned to G. Sometimes called the G violone or great bass viol.

Name: Violone
Description: Large viol with the lowest string tuned to D. Sometimes called the D violone.

Name: Octobass
Description: Extremely large and rare bowed string instrument, essentially a larger version of the double bass.

Name: Nyckelharpa
Description: Swedish bowed instrument with keys to change the pitch of the strings.
